paths.path_name: set_language() no longer stores user language in request.session
paths.description: As of Django 4.0, django.views.i18n.set_language() no longer sets the user language in request.session under the key _language. Code that relies on the session key being populated by set_language() will no longer find it. The text does not state where the language is stored instead.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 3.2 to 4.2 crosses release 4.0, where this behavior was removed.
quotes: django.views.i18n.set_language() doesn't set the user language in request.session (key _language).
conditions.relevance: The change is listed under features removed in 4.0, so a 3.2 -> 4.2 upgrade crosses it.

conditions.statement: The application uses the django.views.i18n.set_language view (e.g. in URL configuration).
quotes: django.views.i18n.set_language() doesn't set the user language in request.session (key _language).
conditions.relevance: The removed behavior only affects applications that use this view.

conditions.statement: The application code reads the _language key from request.session to get the user language.
quotes: doesn't set the user language in request.session (key _language)
conditions.relevance: Code reading request.session['_language'] would not find the value set by set_language() after upgrade.
ambiguities: The text does not state which mechanism replaces the session key for storing the language, nor whether other code depends on the session key.

suggested_actions: Audit code that reads request.session['_language'] (or LANGUAGE_SESSION_KEY) and stop relying on set_language() populating it.
See the Django 3.0 deprecation notes (deprecated-features-3.0) for details on removing usage of this behavior.
